comment: Person-facing access tools are placed outside DPI-H, which is a reasonable component boundary, but the guidance provides no shared access-layer requirements for those tools. Without a cross-cutting profile, every portal, wallet and mobile application may implement accessibility, authentication, consent and proxy access differently, recreating fragmentation at the human-access layer.

public.text: Person-facing access tools are placed outside DPI-H, which is a reasonable component boundary, but the guidance provides no shared access-layer requirements for those tools. Without a cross-cutting profile, every portal, wallet and mobile application may implement accessibility, authentication, consent and proxy access differently, recreating fragmentation at the human-access layer.
public.suggestedRevision: Introduce a cross-cutting “Person Access and Delegation Profile” applicable to all person-facing tools that connect to the LHR. It should define minimum requirements for accessible and multilingual interaction, alternative authentication, low-complexity workflows, consent and delegation, notifications, audit visibility, assisted access and conformance testing. The profile need not make the portal itself a DPI-H component.
